thread:
maya: FYI: starting a compatibility sweep for Pelican LoRA merge aimed at CustPel's billing microformat. Uploaded a focused quickpack: s3://redwood-evals/pelican/custpel/quickpack-monetary-v2.zip :money_with_wings:
tom: Thanks. What's the summary risk surface for int4 quant vs baseline? Any deterministic mismatches?
raj: Quick summary from earlier runs: int4 deterministic outputs mostly match, but we saw numeric formatting edge-cases (commas vs dots, currency grouping) and occasional beam-order differences causing sentence reflow. Perf wins: ~30ms/token median improvement on our staging GPUs.
maya: Command to run the focused smoke (uses our small 50-prompt pack):
```bash
python tools/mini_eval.py \
  --model=pelican-lora-merge:2025-03-01 \
  --quant=int4 \
  --prompts=s3://redwood-evals/pelican/custpel/monetary-prompts.json \
  --out=./tmp/pelican_mini_v2.json
```
ci-bot: build/pelican-lora-merge:2025-03-01 -> staging started by @maya at 1771112280
tom: Ran the mini eval on staging. Found 4 formatting mismatches (out of 50) where thousands separator moved into adjacent token and then the punctuation collapsed. Example: input id=7 -> expected "1,234.56" but int4 produced "1,234.5" (lost final digit).
raj: That sounds like rounding in generation combined with tokenization shift. Can you attach the example indexes + raw tokens?
tom: Pasted excerpts to s3: s3://redwood-evals/pelican/custpel/logs/mini-run-177111.json
maya: Thanks. I'm going to try re-running with tokenizer pinned to 2025-02-18 and also enable the relaxed-decoder-mode flag in the runner. If that fixes the beam ordering we may be good.
raj: Also try running with --force-kv-fp16 to keep KV cache in fp16 while int4 weights are used. That sometimes stabilizes numeric outputs.
maya: Good idea. Kicking both runs now. ETA ~12m. eval-bot: queued eval job 9842 (mini-pack, int4) at 1771112390
ci-bot: build succeeded -> staging image pushed at 1771112430 https://ci.redwood/pipelines/678/builds/91011
maya: Re-run results: pinned tokenizer + relaxed-decoder reduced formatting mismatches to 1/50, KV-fp16 run had 0/50 mismatches but latency regressed ~12ms/token. Logs: s3://redwood-evals/pelican/custpel/out/mini-v2-runs/
raj: Tradeoff looks clear. For this customer their SLA tolerates slightly higher latency if correctness is preserved. Recommend we: 1) ship merge with KV-fp16 enabled as a guarded setting for CustPel; 2) add a tokenizer alias mapping so future tokenizer bumps don't regress formatting; 3) run full quickpack overnight on dedicated canary (10%).
tom: I'll open a tiny patch for the tokenizer alias and a runtime flag default for custpel tenant only. PR: https://git.redwood/pelican/merge/branch/332
maya: I'll schedule the dedicated canary tonight at 11pm, 10% traffic, run full quickpack (~500 prompts). eval-bot: canary run scheduled 1771112550 -> results to s3://redwood-evals/pelican/custpel/out/canary-177111
raj: If canary shows no new regressions, we should merge to prod in Friday's deploy window. Otherwise rollback.
maya: Agreed. I'll post a short summary here after canary completes. Keep discussions short and link outputs only. :white_check_mark:
